title: A Moment of Peace
subtitle: I could never think of leaving. Let that song drift away to Tuscany!

trails.title: Picnic Blanket
trails.description: There's food on the picnic blanket, yet no one is around. Perhaps the observation record will tell you what happened.

content.text:
"According to the Observer Instruction Book, we've met the conditions for terminating the observation."
"But the picnic is not over yet ... Do we have to go?"
"I'm afraid it's not an option. Now, Ms. Sotheby, Mr. APPLe, I need you to focus. You'll be leaving the stage at any time ... Hello, Mr. APPLe?"
"He's not responding. Oh no, is he poisoned again? Should I make an antidote?!"
"No need. I think he's just drunk."
"But X said if an observer ended an observation when unconscious, they might be directly transferred to another observation. I think we'd better wake him up, Ms. Sotheby."
"Mr. APPLe? Wake up! We need to ..."
"No ..."

items.text: What happened after that?
Street, Florence

items.speaker: Citizen I
items.text: The treasure hunters must have opened the secret chamber and found the Compliners' relics, right?

items.speaker: Book Merchant
items.text: Well, there was no treasure inside. Just a few letters and a painter's address.

items.speaker: Citizen II
items.text: That's it? Wh-What about all those symbols? Don't tell me you made it all up!

items.speaker: Book Merchant
items.text: Easy, easy, allow me to continue ... Long after the poor painters and artisans scattered to the wind.

items.speaker: Book Merchant
items.text: Each of them received a special pigment from Uccello. They used it on other projects they worked on, leaving their "signatures"—these symbols behind to mark their work.

items.speaker: Book Merchant
items.text: And so concludes our Firenze fresco mystery! To celebrate this touching story, I've hired a team of talented artists to reproduce their paintings in a new book, and I gave it a wonderful title:

items.speaker: Book Merchant
items.text: "La Primavera di Firenze!" (The Spring in Florence!)
The crowd lets out a chorus of dissatisfaction.

items.speaker: Citizen I
items.text: What a disappointment ...

items.speaker: Citizen II
items.text: And a lousy title.

items.speaker: Book Merchant
items.text: Oh, umm, I-I've got something even better here! A map straight from the Spanish court with a direct route to India! Think of the opportunities that await you!
Hidden relics, missing artists ... No matter the season, you'll hear all kinds of legends in Florence just minutes after you arrive.
Perhaps everyone who has ever lived here is destined to become a legend themselves.
In the midst of the bustle, the Tuscan sun has quietly begun to sink below the horizon.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Achoo!

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: I have a serious question: what is there in India that is worth all this fuss? If Marco Polo is to be believed, not even there can one escape the troublesome rumors of merchants and courtiers.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Unfortunately, humanity's thirst for gossip knows neither geographical nor temporal boundaries.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: But this APPLe still finds it so strange that all the rumors about these Compliners turned out to be false, from top to bottom. Seems like, no matter the era, lies always travel faster than the truth ...

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Well, I wouldn't say that. In fact, the rumors didn't really hold much weight until you arrived.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Huh?
The Assassin gazes out at the distant crimson clouds.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: The Compliner's relics weren't the most important thing we were searching for; in fact we were looking for an apple, one very much like you.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: So when you turned up, looking like the very apple we had lost, it was only natural for us—and the Templars—to keep an eye on you.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Of course, it turns out you weren't the apple we were looking for.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: And you're only telling me this NOW? I thought we were friends.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: It's only because I consider you friends that I had to keep this from you.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: That apple brings bloodshed and war wherever it appears.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Hmm. Well, then it does sound like quite the troublesome thing.
The Assassin smiles.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: You've caused quite a stir in Firenze yourself—no need to be modest.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Correct! You are an amazing apple in your own right! My only regret is that I never got the chance to dissect you and study your inner workings.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: I hope you don't mind, but I think you may have to keep that regret forever—ahh!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Ms. Sotheby, why did you sneak up on me like that?!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: I did not! I just wanted to tell you that Vertin and I met an old gentleman down there who was kind enough to give us directions! Well, he said if we keep heading northwest along the Arno River, and then ... umm ...

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Anyway, we'd end up in Pratovecchio eventually!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: I do believe you may have skipped some—if not all—of the necessary information.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Ezio knows the way. All we need to do now is deliver the letter to Mr. Uccello.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: I suppose we must say goodbye to our dear Firenze for now.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: That red is so vibrant! Like an endless field of poppies!
It carries the brilliance and hope of the renaissance.
The red flows across the sky in a rosy stream, passing through the window flower boxes hanging over Florentine streets until it pours into the winding Arno River.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: What did I say? This place has the best view!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It is positively gorgeous. I see why you insisted we all come up here together.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: A place of beauty like this is a fitting place for farewells ...
Before saying goodbye, the soft whispers between friends fade into the coming night's breeze, melting with the golden glow of the setting sun.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: By the way, I had a discussion with some of my fellow painters. We discovered that Pratovecchio is rich in a special mineral—

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: One need only grind and heat it properly ... then presto!

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: You have yourself some invisible pigment!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: So that's the source of the pigment used in the fresco?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Uccello was born in Pratovecchio. It's safe to assume he brought some from his hometown to Florence.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Just a hint of this powder and you are able to create a vast array of remarkable colors.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Among them, the most famous is a color some call "Firenze Red."

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: "Firenze Red" ...
A red that isn't too glaring or gaudy.
You see it on the rooftops of the houses, the reflections on the rivers at dusk, and even on the signs of street-side shops ...
It's no wonder many praise Florence and its magnificent red.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: It's a good name.
One week later
Countryside, Pratovecchio
The bumpy journey has finally come to an end.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Phew, finally. That darling little house up ahead must be Mr. Uccello's home!
A small farmhouse stands beneath the thick shade of olive trees ahead, the stone walls glowing white in the afternoon sun.
The young lady takes a few excited strides ahead, then pauses.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: *weep*

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: I just realized something. When he learns from us that his friend Bianca has been dead for years, he might be very sad!

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Mr. Uccello, if he's even still alive, will be an old man by now.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: A man of his age grows familiar with death and farewells.
The Assassin gently pats Sotheby.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Let's go.
He steps forward, pushing open the vine-covered gate.
Garden

items.speaker: Strange Woman
items.text: Oh! Who are you? Where did you pop up from?!
The small courtyard is vibrant with life, and a woman with paint stains covering her dress stands alone in the sunlight.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Apologies for the intrusion, miss. My name is Ezio Auditore from Firenze.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: We're here looking for Paolo Uccello. We have a letter here addressed to him from one of his friends.

items.speaker: Strange Woman
items.text: Friends ...? I'm not sure my father would agree he had any friends.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Is that so? Well, the letter is signed "Bianca."

items.speaker: Strange Woman
items.text: Bianca! You should have said so earlier! Please, put the letter down; it's meant for me.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Hmm? The letter mentions a particular piece of stained glass and details of the fresco in the Florence Cathedral; we assumed it must have been meant for Mr. Uccello.
The woman looks wistfully in the direction they came, then laughs as if recalling a joyful memory.

items.speaker: Strange Woman
items.text: Pfff. It appears I've deceived you as well.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: Allow me to introduce myself. I am Antonia Uccello.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: And perhaps the "Uccello" you friendly strangers are looking for.
Antonia's Home

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: I see ... So Bianca has passed away, too.
Her paint-covered hands grip the yellowed papers tightly.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: That fresco was the last work we did together.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: Father passed away soon after, leaving behind my sick mother and a pile of debts.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: I used to follow Father wherever he went, whatever job he took—sculpture, masonry, painting frescoes ... everything. I learned all I could from him and, after he died, hoped to accept commissions independently. But as a woman, it was almost impossible.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: But once I left Firenze and began using Father's name to make a living some of his old patrons were kind enough to keep sending work my way, provided I concealed my true identity.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Oh, so you're the imposter!
Antonia gives the impertinent artist a glare.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: I admit, I tried to imitate Father's style in my earlier works, but I'm much more than just an imposter now.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: No, no, no ... a painter's mind should be a mirror—capturing and reflecting the truth and beauty of nature.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: To simply copy the works of another? No, miss, it seems you still have much to learn.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: Hah!

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: Is that what you think? Well, I've heard it all before!

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: "Minds as a mirror"? Ridiculous. Let me tell you: a painter's mind should be like a sheet of transparent glass.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: It refracts and transforms the external world, then reconstructs its image inside the painter's brain, rather than simply copying the natural world around us.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: Oh, hmm, that is an intriguing theory ... odd perhaps but not without merit ...

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: You just wait here. I'll show you with one of my recent works.
She springs up and begins rummaging through a nearby stack of sheets.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: She seems so full of life.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: She reminds me of my sister. Women like her have seen much pain, but they never let it defeat them.

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: *sigh* If only her understanding of painting were a bit more profound. I believe we might become good friends.
Sun rays pour through the patterned window, and the light spots dance merrily on the old wooden floor.
The pot on the stove gurgles as the fresh scent of herbs fills the room.
War, plague, poverty; the loss of loved ones—painful memories of the older generation now linger in the cracks of the walls and beneath the leaves of the trees.
Antonia has lived in this quiet refuge for a long time.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: Pardon me, may I ask ... what was your name again?
Antonia has returned, holding a yellowed sketch in her hands.
She looks closely at Ezio, studying his face.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: You said you are an Auditore, right?

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Yes. You know about my family?

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: I thought so; you look so familiar ...

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: I'm sure you know your mother, Maria Auditore, funded my father for a time?

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: Father conducted a lot of his research on perspective and lighting. He passed that knowledge on to me.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: I see ... And you applied that knowledge to your frescoes, huh?
The artist winks playfully.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: What goes around comes around, right?

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Architects, sponsors, painters, artisans, assassins, outsiders ... Our identities may differ, but our actions are all deeply interconnected!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Ah, this APPLe has never felt so moved by the warmth and power of community.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: I heard a lot about your family from Father. He was always very grateful to you.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: I'm sorry, if Mother hadn't cut your funding, perhaps you wouldn't have had to ...
Antonia shakes her head calmly.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: Your family helped us more than we could have ever asked for.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: Your mother once commissioned my father to paint a family portrait. Do you remember?

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Family portrait ...? No, I had no idea.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: It was many years ago, and the painting was never finished ... because of what happened to your family.
She moves slowly then purposefully toward Ezio and hands him the sketch.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: This is the only draft left. But I believe it should be returned to you.

items.speaker: Antonia
items.text: Consider it a token of thanks for delivering this letter all the way from Firenze!

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Thank you.
Ezio takes the sketch, gently unfolding it in his hands.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: This is ...
On the yellowed sketch paper, a roughly drawn portrait captures all the members of the Auditore family.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Father, Mother, Federico, Claudia, Petruccio ...

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: This draft captures the younger version of you perfectly—I can vouch for that!
The young Ezio in the painting stands off to the side with a casual stance.
Without a care in the world, the 17-year-old boy with an errant heart eager to explore and venture without restraints.
The rest of the family didn't seem to mind him. They stood against the clear Tuscan sky, their faces glowing with dignified poise.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Ah, what a lovely family portrait; even the weather looks lovely. The painter did a great job capturing a wonderful moment.
Almost imperceptibly, Ezio's hands tremble, overwhelmed by a flood of long-held back emotions.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: One of the sweetest of my life.
From somewhere or perhaps nowhere, he hears familiar laughter in the distance.
As light as the breeze, sweeping across the red rooftops, traveling over the river of time, and finally slipping out from the yellowed sketch.
It is a good life we lead, brother.
The best. May it never change.
And may it never change us.
The brothers talked about something else afterward. Was it about grappa or the bank? Or was it about the beautiful Cristina?
The gentle and warm memory scatters with the wind, eventually melting in the afternoon sunlight.
The young Auditore still remembers how they used to laugh and cry like innocent children; the entire world was waiting for them to explore.
A Moment of Peace for the Auditore.
